second_order: building, repairing, and rebuilding the Yak together
theme_note: These codes share the practice of contributing people and pixels to make the Yak exist and keep it present. Within it, participants divide the first design, place and revisit pixels, repair damage, celebrate completion, rebuild, and rally whoever is available; batch 02 extends the practice from the first build into overnight rebuilding.

second_order: keeping pixel work on one picture and coordinates
theme_note: These codes hold together because participants keep distributed pixel work aligned to a shared visual and location. What varies is the object of alignment: the white border, the original before a second Yak, a mirrored plan, one coordinate map at a time, a new empty site, or a reminder of which picture to build.

second_order: fighting, mourning, and joking through lost Yaks
theme_note: These codes share participants responding to overwriting and loss rather than merely building. Their responses vary from warnings, defensive design and vigilance to revenge language, mourning time spent, RIP memorials, rehabilitation jokes, and recounting a half-built Yak erased by suspected bots.

second_order: making truces and moving the Yak for neighbors
theme_note: These codes share the practice of finding room through relocation and dealings with neighboring projects. Within it, participants reframe apparent griefing as overlap, exchange apologies and preservation help, redirect after refusal, answer relocation requests, offer reciprocal drawing or rebuilding, negotiate overlap and peace, and move some negotiation to Discord.

second_order: turning the Yak effort into a good shared story
theme_note: These codes share participants making a collective account of the finished effort. The account varies between announcing the end and thanking the breeding program, making the remnant findable, imagining a time-lapse, praising the effort, and remembering repeated moves as exciting and fun; batch 02 supplies most of this retrospective practice.

These two codes share participants encountering the event's mechanics rather than coordinating the drawing itself. One abandons an appeal after refreshing a bugged canvas; the other asks how the event works at all.
